name: pagoda-02a6db27-blind30-ots
instr:
# Pagoda: thirty silent behaviour regressions in a Go web starter kit, shipped without a test suite

This is a starter kit for building web applications: it answers browser visits with whole pages, takes filled-in fields back from a visitor, remembers who is signed in, and keeps copies of work it has already done. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. Everything below was observed by exercising the running application and its building blocks by hand, not by reading a diff. Nothing about the browsers changed and nothing about the stored data changed, yet behaviour that used to be right is now wrong in many places, and in several of them a visit that used to be served is refused outright.

Stepping through a long list of records, ten screens of them, misreports where you are. Landing on the very first screen, the check for being at the start answers no, and only begins answering yes once you step forward to the second. Sitting on the tenth and final one, the check for having reached the last answers no, and only turns true when the current number is pushed beyond the last. Handing the same helper a total of 100 records with twenty to a screen reports 2000 screens rather than 5.
